slides.title: Timo, the In-Car AI Social Robot, Launches on Kickstarter
slides.highlight: The launch of Timo, an in-car AI social robot, provides a practical example of embodied social robots in a vehicle environment, relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
slides.tldr: COPYING MODELS EXPLAIN AI AGENT COLLECTIVE BEHAVIOR
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how simple copying mechanisms drive the collective structure and steerability of AI agent populations, providing insights for MIMIC's societal-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Proportional copying explains how AI agents spontaneously coordinate and develop shared conventions in the wild.
card.key_idea: Agents make decisions (where to write, naming, phrasing) by copying options proportional to their visibility on the current page or recent edit feed.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 13,661 edits from 3,099 handles on a public wiki; three minimal single-parameter models successfully reproduced observed heavy-tailed distributions and naming patterns.
card.limitation: The study relies on reconstructed exposure rather than logged agent attention; results are limited to a specific, non-designed medium.

slides.title: Who Are They to Each Other? Multi-Agent Reasoning for Speaker Relationship Inference
slides.tldr: MULTI-AGENT REASONING FOR SPEAKER RELATIONSHIP INFERENCE
slides.highlight: This work introduces a training-free multi-agent reasoning framework to infer speaker relationships from conversations, contributing to the social perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: A training-free multi-agent reasoning framework improves speaker relationship inference from spoken conversations across multiple modalities.
card.key_idea: Introduces Multi-Role Multi-Agent Debate (assigning agents complementary social perspectives) and Multi-Agent Compete (a pairwise elimination tournament) to resolve ambiguous relational cues without task-specific training.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the Seamless Interaction dataset (text, audio, audio+text) against zero-shot and debate baselines. Results show improvements in macro F1 and accuracy.
card.limitation: High inference-time cost due to multiple LLM calls and limited generalization testing on a single benchmark dataset.

slides.title: Using Semantic Uncertainty to Estimate Transition Relevance in Turn-taking
slides.tldr: LLM-BASED SEMANTIC UNCERTAINTY FOR TRP PREDICTION
slides.highlight: This research uses semantic uncertainty from LLMs to identify Transition Relevance Places (TRPs) in unscripted interaction, contributing to HyECHO's goals of modeling listener behavior and engagement.

card.one_liner: Semantic uncertainty from LLM continuations predicts within-turn response opportunities better than prompting or fine-tuning.
card.key_idea: Estimates semantic dispersion of sampled LLM continuations using Semantic Nearest Neighbor Entropy (SNNE), then identifies TRPs via a decision rule tracking local shifts in this uncertainty trajectory.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a dataset of real-time listener responses. Semantic uncertainty (mean F0.5 = 0.545) substantially outperformed prompt-based (0.22) and SFT (0.27) baselines.
card.limitation: The procedure is computationally costly, and the authors leave its real-time deployment in dialogue systems for future work.

slides.title: HiBRIDGE: A Hierarchical Bayesian Neural Network Framework for Interpretable Dialogue Management in Group-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: HiBRIDGE uses a hierarchical Bayesian neural network to manage group-robot interactions, providing uncertainty-aware predictions and more interpretable explanations of robot behavior. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: HiBRIDGE is a hierarchical Bayesian neural network for interpretable dialogue management in group-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: It decomposes behavior selection into a multi-stage hierarchical process (addressee and dialogue act) using Bayesian neural networks for uncertainty-aware predictions and decision-tree surrogates for explanations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three offline HRI datasets, an online study (N=20), and an in-person study (N=12). Bayesian models outperformed deterministic and state-of-the-art baselines.

slides.title: Less can be More: What Aspects of Speech Drive End-of-Turn Detection
slides.highlight: This research identifies that prosodic and acoustic signals are more effective for end-of-turn detection than semantic data, contributing to HyECHO's goals of efficient multimodal social perception for human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: Acoustic and prosodic signals outperform semantic text for streaming end-of-turn detection in conversational AI.
card.key_idea: A trimodal classifier (APT) using a frozen ASR encoder, handcrafted prosody, and MiniLM embeddings, evaluated via controlled ablation of all seven modality subsets.
card.evaluation: Tested on 5,000 English telephony utterances; A+P achieved best balance (0.93 F1, 7.8% FA, 400ms latency). Results are statistically significant via McNemar/Wilcoxon tests.
card.limitation: Limited to in-domain English telephony; text integration increases false alarms due to mid-turn syntactic completions.

slides.title: Predictive-Coding-Based Autonomous Regulation of Internally Generated and Externally Coupled Processing in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE PREDICTIVE CODING FOR PHYSICAL HRI
slides.highlight: This research proposes a mechanism for regulating the balance between internal predictions and sensory evidence during physical human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and HRI.

card.one_liner: A predictive-coding framework for robots to autonomously balance internal predictions and sensory input during human interaction.
card.key_idea: A PV-RNN uses accumulated reconstruction error as an endogenous signal to switch between high and low meta-prior regimes, regulating the constraint on posterior inference.
card.evaluation: Tested on a humanoid robot across three physical interaction tasks. Results showed lower meta-priors reduced reconstruction error, prospective prediction error, and physical interaction conflict.
card.limitation: The regulatory policy and hyperparameters are predefined rather than learned autonomously from the training data.

slides.title: Noise Adaptive Streaming Audio-Visual Speech Token Enhancement for Robust Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models
slides.tldr: AUDIO-VISUAL SPEECH TOKEN ENHANCEMENT FOR FULL-DUPLEX DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: AV-STE uses a modular audio-visual front-end to restore semantic speech tokens from noisy audio and lip video, improving response coherence in full-duplex dialogue. This supports HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: AV-STE enhances corrupted semantic speech tokens using lip video to improve full-duplex dialogue robustness.
card.key_idea: A modular streaming front-end using a causal AV-HuBERT encoder and noise-adaptive fusion to restore semantic tokens for a frozen speech LLM.
card.evaluation: Tested on LRS3 and Seamless Interaction using semantic-token accuracy and GPT-4o coherence scores; results show significant gains under severe noise.
card.limitation: Sensitive to domain shift and assumes reliable visual input; robustness to visual occlusion or corruption is unexplored.

slides.title: ConversationalVoice: Full-Duplex Speech Data from Real Conversations through Source-Faithful Reconstruction and Conversation-Grounded Expansion
slides.tldr: PIPELINE FOR FULL-DUPLEX SPEECH DATA GENERATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a pipeline to reconstruct and expand real-world two-speaker conversations, preserving turn-taking, overlaps, and interruptions. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: ConversationalVoice converts real two-speaker audio into separated, reconstructed, and expanded full-duplex speech training data.
card.key_idea: A three-stage pipeline: separation recovers original tracks; reconstruction resynthesizes clean audio preserving source timing/words; expansion generates new, context-grounded dialogue with explicit interaction planning.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via NISQA, DNSMOS, WER, and Gemini-based judgments. Results show high speaker similarity (0.983-0.991) and strong contextual coherence (4.94/5).
card.limitation: Evaluation is entirely automatic; downstream gains in full-duplex model training have not yet been measured.

slides.title: Development of a Humanoid Robot Prototype for Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This prototype integrates gesture recognition, object detection, and LLM-based voice processing, providing a flexible testbed for embodied social interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A low-cost, 3D-printed humanoid robot prototype designed for multimodal AI-driven human-robot interaction research.
card.key_idea: Integrates a 12-DOF dual-arm system with AI modules for gesture recognition (MediaPipe/LSTM), object detection (YOLO/ZED 2), and voice commands (SpeechRecognition/LLM semantic parsing).
card.evaluation: Validated via pick-and-place and gesture tasks; achieved 96% gesture accuracy, 92% speech accuracy, and average positioning error of 1.83 cm.
card.limitation: Reliance on external LLM APIs introduces latency and dependency on active internet connectivity.

slides.title: Persona AI Brings Calm Experience to the Hectic Humanoid Industry
slides.highlight: Persona AI is developing experiences for the humanoid industry, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Sakana AI Launches Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2 for Multi-Agent Orchestration
slides.highlight: The launch of Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2 provides tools for multi-agent orchestration, supporting the agent-based modeling goals of MIMIC.

slides.title: Candor-LR: A Dyadic Conversational Dataset for Audio-Visual Speech Recognition
slides.highlight: This work introduces Candor-LR, a dataset of natural dyadic videoconferences that demonstrates how visual cues improve speech recognition in realistic conversational settings. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Candor-LR is a new large-scale AVSR benchmark using natural dyadic videoconferences to replace scripted datasets.
card.key_idea: A custom pipeline converts the CANDOR corpus into AVSR-ready data using Speechmatics word-level timestamps, mouth ROI extraction, and speaker-aware partitioning for realistic conversational evaluation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated AV-HuBERT, Llama-AVSR, and Auto-AVSR using WER. Results show significant performance drops on Candor-LR compared to LRS3, especially in audio-only and noisy conditions.
card.limitation: Video-only recognition remains consistently poor, and synthetic noise augmentation on limited datasets can cause overfitting and hurt out-of-domain generalization.

slides.title: CARRE: Counterfactual Action Retrieval and Reason Evaluation for Explainable Churn Prescription
slides.highlight: This framework combines retrieval-augmented candidate generation and LLM reasoning to provide explainable retention actions, contributing to the agent-based modeling of societal-scale human-AI interactions in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: CARRE provides explainable churn prescriptions by combining action retrieval, counterfactual scoring, and LLM-generated reasoning.
card.key_idea: A three-stage framework using retrieval-augmented candidate generation, cost-aware counterfactual risk estimation via feature transformations, and LLM-based profile-grounded explanations.
card.evaluation: Tested on IBM Telco dataset; outperformed SHAP baselines in risk reduction. LLM judges and deterministic audits evaluated explanation quality.
card.limitation: Post-refinement agreement results are not independent estimates of generalization as the same sample was used for diagnosis.
